questions.question: Orient verdicts are in the trace: BK-423 and BK-414/BK-420 constrain the rewrite (they get named in the RFC), while BK-384, BK-397 and BK-366 are unrelated. Two lines outside the RFC go stale the moment it merges: BK-418's backlog body says "Four interventions are unmeasured", and report.md § Run B baseline says the route choice is "settled when RFC-0020 is rewritten; until then the RFC's rule is the one in force". What scope should this PR have?

options.label: RFC + two stale lines (Recommended)
options.description: Rewrite RFC-0020, plus the trace and both decision logs. Also correct BK-418's body to "rule (c) is unmeasured, run B tests it", and turn the report's 'until then' sentence into a pointer to the RFC's decision rule. That keeps the repo matching reality at this commit (principle 3), costs about four lines, and grows no process file.

options.label: RFC text only, as framed
options.description: Only the RFC, the trace and the logs. The backlog body and the report sentence stay stale until a later PR, and run B's session reads them as written.

options.label: RFC + backlog line only
options.description: Fix BK-418's body, but leave report.md alone, since the research record is a dated record. The report's 'until then' sentence then points at a rule that no longer exists.

questions.question: CI's docs job on #1111 fails because pymdown-extensions 12.2 (on PyPI since 13:01 today) breaks mkdocstrings' Highlighter. I reproduced it locally: 12.2 fails, 12.1 builds. It's a transitive dependency, unpinned in pyproject.toml, so master and every docs-touching PR are affected, not only this one. How should I handle it?

options.label: Separate hotfix PR (Recommended)
options.description: Mint one BUG item (an exception to the brief's no-new-IDs rule). Open a small PR that adds `pymdown-extensions!=12.2` to the docs dependency group, with the reproduction in its body, and merge that first. Then rerun #1111's CI unchanged, so #1111 stays RFC-only.

options.label: Pin inside #1111
options.description: Add the `!=12.2` exclusion to pyproject.toml in this PR. That gets #1111 green fastest, but an RFC-text PR then carries a dependency change, which breaks its scope and the brief's 'RFC text only'.

options.label: Wait for upstream
options.description: Change nothing, watch for a pymdown-extensions 12.2.1 or a mkdocstrings fix, and rerun CI. #1111 stays red for an unknown time, and the trace's review: block (which needs green CI) waits with it.

#1111 is behind master now that #1112 has merged, and its CI only goes green on a commit that includes the pin. How should I bring it up to date?

options.label: Rebase + force-push (Recommended)
options.description: Run `git rebase origin/master`, then `git push --force-with-lease`. History stays linear and CI reruns on the new head. The review threads are already resolved, so moving their lines costs nothing.

options.label: Merge master in
options.description: Add a merge commit from master, so no force-push is needed. The PR history gets a merge commit, which the squash merge removes anyway.
